summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29% YoY to Rs 3,335.2 crore, with adjusted EBITDA up 34% to Rs 232.2 crore and a record Rs 543 crore of new business wins.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 28.7% YoY and 10% QoQ to Rs 3,335.2 crore, both segments grew double digits. Adjusted EBITDA rose 34% YoY to Rs 232.2 crore with margin up 30 bps to about 7%, and adjusted PBT rose to Rs 32.1 crore from Rs 18.8 crore. ISCS EBITDA margin dipped to 8.1% from 9.3% in Q4 on onboarding costs for new contracts, while GFS margin improved to 4.1%. Reported PAT fell to Rs 22.5 crore from Rs 71.1 crore because Q1 FY26 included an InvIT gain; operational PAT rose 156% to Rs 8.8 crore.

segments.name: ISCS (Integrated Supply Chain Solutions)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 2,417 crore, +21.9% YoY, with India and Europe growing on new wins and North America aided by a large project live last year. Adjusted EBITDA Rs 196.3 crore at 8.1% margin, down from 9.3% in Q4 due to transition costs on new contracts.

segments.name: GFS (Global Forwarding Solutions)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 918 crore, +50.6% YoY, driven by ocean freight volumes in India and higher freight rates. EBITDA margin 4.1% vs 2.1% a year ago, helped by volume growth, cost optimisation and better sourcing.

guidance_outlook: Aspiration of mid-teens revenue growth for FY27; management expects profit growth to outpace revenue growth.
ISCS margin to return to above 9% in Q2 FY27 (management 'fairly confident'), and 9.5% to 10% by Q4 FY27 per CFO.
Group PBT margin aspiration of 4% (about 3% PAT at 25% tax); management said FY27 year-end is an aspiration, FY28 is the firm target.
GFS EBITDA margin expected at 4.5% to 5% over time, with at least 5% needed to reach group targets; GFS margins expected to stay around current levels while growth moderates to high double digits.
Early-teens EBITDA margin target referenced; Q2 first 45 days described as tracking similarly to Q1.
H2 expected to be stronger than H1, with Q4 typically strongest.
ALA JV defence and aerospace revenue to start in H2 FY27; aspiration of about Rs 2,000 crore revenue by year 5.
capex_capacity: Warehouse utilisation is about 85% by management's estimate, with room to improve through racking and automation investment.
Roughly 25 million sq ft of warehousing capacity cited by an analyst; management did not dispute the figure.
Acquisition of Swamy & Sons 3PL completed in Q1; results include 40 days of its performance and integration is on track.
Oracle ERP implemented for India ISCS business; transport management solution integrated with customers and vendors.
Additional space taken for new business wins, raising right-of-use depreciation to Rs 114 crore (from Rs 93 crore YoY) and lease interest to Rs 26 crore (from Rs 20 crore).
demand_pricing: New business wins of Rs 543 crore in Q1 (vs Rs 524 crore in Q4), about two-thirds from existing customers and one-third from new logos.
Order pipeline at Rs 7,500 crore plus, up from Rs 6,100 crore; management expects 20% to 25% conversion over 12 to 18 months, in line with track record.

Wins include a renewable energy provider, a kitchen appliances maker, a consumer beverages company and a premium motorcycle maker in Europe in ISCS; GFS wins include a sustainable packaging company and a telecom equipment provider.
Fuel cost increases are contractually passed through to customers with some time lag; container and air freight cost increases are also passed on under contracts.
Management said FX has limited impact on profitability because revenue and costs are both in local markets.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ISCS EBITDA fall in Q1 despite higher revenue, and when will margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed the dip to onboarding and transition costs on contracts added in Q4 and Q1, plus Q4 benefited from customer price corrections. Management expects ISCS margin back to 9% in Q2 and 9.5% to 10% by Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How long does a new ISCS contract take to reach stable margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 1 to 2 quarters: finished-goods or aftermarket contracts take about 1 quarter, while sub-assembly or implant-heavy contracts can take about 2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Were GFS margins helped by one-offs linked to the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gains reflect volume growth, new wins and vendor consolidation, and it expects GFS growth to moderate to high double digits with margins broadly holding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ALA JV's revenue potential and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about Rs 2,000 crore revenue in year 5, with first revenue in H2 FY27 after warehouse certification, and expects it to be margin accretive given high entry barriers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company pushing growth at the expense of margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prioritises profitable growth, that all wins are margin accretive, and that profit growth should exceed revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the Middle East and Africa?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is in discussions with Middle East companies and prefers a partnership route; no entry announced yet, and it is taking extra precautions because of the war.

risks_watch: Recession risk from supply chain disruption and geopolitical events, including the war situation; management says it has not yet seen this playing out.
Manpower availability by geography, which management said is a full-year risk, with cost increases passed on to customers.
Container and air freight capacity tightness and rate volatility in GFS.
ISCS margin recovery to 9% in Q2 depends on onboarding costs rolling off; the Q2 target is management's expectation, not guidance.
Depreciation and lease costs rising with new space (ROU depreciation and lease interest up YoY), which could weigh on PBT.
Reported PAT comparisons are distorted by the Q1 FY26 InvIT gain.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and wins, and openly acknowledges the ISCS margin dip as transitional. Less firm on timing: the 4% PBT margin is framed as a FY27 aspiration, with FY28 as the firm commitment.

I would say that in the 12 to 15 or 18-month period, definitely a similar conversion of 20% to 25%, we should be able to achieve.
We very firmly believe in profitable growth. We are not a company that will run after growth ignoring the profits.
But FY '28, definitely, we will be achieving our aspiration of 4%.

growth.why: Management aspires to mid-teens FY27 revenue growth (cut from prior), backed by a Rs 543 cr record quarterly win and a Rs 7,500 cr+ pipeline (20-25% conversion over 12-18 months), plus ~85% warehouse utilisation with room via racking/automation; no specific new capacity or capex quantified, and FY27 margin/PBT targets are aspirational with FY28 the firm target.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: ISCS margin guided back above 9% in Q2 FY27 from 8.1% in Q1 (Q4 FY26 was 9.3%) and 9.5% to 10% by Q4 FY27 per CFO; GFS margin 4.1% vs 2.1% a year ago, with 4.5% to 5% targeted but at least 5% needed for group targets.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No greenfield capacity quantified; Swamy & Sons 3PL acquired in Q1 (40 days in results) and extra leased space taken, with ROU depreciation up to Rs 114 cr from Rs 93 cr, but no new facility size or date given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Record Rs 543 cr new business wins (21% of quarterly revenue) and pipeline of Rs 7,500 cr+ (up from Rs 6,100 cr) at 20-25% conversion over 12-18 months; revenue grew 28.7% YoY in Q1 but mid-teens FY27 aspiration is below that pace.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Warehouse utilisation about 85% per management, above the 80% threshold, with room to improve via racking and automation, but no specific capex amount or date was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenue growth aspiration was cut to mid-teens for FY27 and the 4% PBT margin is framed as an FY27 aspiration with FY28 the firm target, so no upgrade signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 PBT margin and revenue targets are aspirational, the ISCS 9% Q2 recovery is management expectation not guidance, and manpower availability is a full-year risk, though Q2 first 45 days are tracking like Q1.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: ALA JV defence and aerospace revenue is set to start in H2 FY27 after warehouse certification, with a Rs 2,000 cr year-5 aspiration; this is a new vertical rather than a product launch.

rows.label: ALA JV defence and aerospace revenue
rows.why: First revenue from the ALA JV in H2 FY27 after warehouse certification, with about Rs 2,000 cr revenue targeted by year 5 and expected to be margin accretive.

rows.label: Record new business wins and pipeline
rows.why: Rs 543 cr of wins in Q1 (all-time high, up from Rs 524 cr in Q4) and Rs 7,500 cr+ pipeline; 20-25% conversion expected over 12-18 months.

rows.label: Profit growth to outpace revenue growth
rows.why: Management said all wins are margin accretive and profit should grow faster than revenue; Q1 adjusted PBT rose 70.7% YoY to Rs 32.1 cr on revenue growth of 28.7%.

tone.note: Management was confident on record wins, the Rs 7,500 cr pipeline and ISCS margin recovery, but cautious on timing, framing the 4% PBT margin as an FY27 aspiration with FY28 the firm target.
